item.title: The DevCon MCP Workshop Now Speaks .NET
item.description:
The DevCon MCP Workshop Now Speaks .NET sajith.subrama…

22 Jul 2026

Sajith Subramanian
Poyraz Yildirim

Share

The hands-on Model Context Protocol (MCP) workshop from DevCon 2026 now ships with a complete C# / .NET track, sitting side by side with the original Node.js content. If you build on .NET, you can now work through the entire workshop end-to-end without leaving your language of choice — the code, the tooling, and the docs are all there.

What is the MCP Workshop?

The workshop is a guided, seven-step journey that takes you from a bare MCP server all the way to a production-ready agent grounded in real Autodesk Platform Services (APS) APIs:

  • Build an MCP server and connect it to VS Code and GitHub Copilot.
  • Extend it with external tools — a filesystem tool and a live weather API.
  • Connect to the Autodesk Platform Services (APS) API using 2-legged OAuth to list and create OSS buckets.
  • Add 3-legged OAuth so your agent can call APS APIs on behalf of a signed-in user.
  • Build your own MCP client and wire in an LLM to create a fully autonomous agent.

Until now, every step was written for Node.js. With this release, every step is also written for .NET.

What's in the .NET Track?

The .NET track is purely additive — nothing in the existing Node.js experience changed. What's new:

  • Language-tabbed docs. Every chapter now has switchable Node.js and .NET code tabs, so you can follow whichever runtime you prefer with a single click.
  • Seven .NET code snapshots. A complete `-dotnet` code state for each stage of the workshop, from the first `add` and `greet` tools to the full APS-connected agent — so you can jump in at any step.
  • Modern .NET foundations. The server is built on ASP.NET Core and the official `ModelContextProtocol.AspNetCore` SDK, targeting .NET 10, with tools declared through clean `McpServerTool` attributes.
  • Full APS integration in C#. 2-legged and 3-legged OAuth, OSS bucket operations, a custom MCP client, and an interactive agent with an AEC-focused system prompt — all in idiomatic C#.

Where to Find It

The complete source code is available on GitHub: autodesk-platform-services/mcp-devcon2026

Whether you're a longtime .NET developer or just curious how MCP fits into the C# world, there's never been a better time to build your first agent on Autodesk Platform Services.

item.title: Forma Takeoff API Classification and Sheet Reference Migration/Deprecation Announcement
item.description:
Forma Takeoff API Classification and Sheet Reference Migration/Deprecation Announcement zhong.wu@autod…

23 Jul 2026

Zhong Wu
Robert Morgan

Share

Safe Harbor Statement:

The features and timelines described below are forward-looking and subject to change. This notice is provided for planning purposes only and is not a commitment, promise, or legal obligation to deliver any material, code, or functionality. Do not rely on this information when making purchasing decisions.

Autodesk continues to evolve the Preconstruction platform and its APIs. As part of this work, Takeoff is transitioning classification management to the Forma Classifications Service and updating how classification and sheet reference data are exposed through the Takeoff API.

Autodesk will begin migrating projects soon. As each project is migrated, its existing Takeoff classification systems will be recreated in the Forma Classifications Service, and the Takeoff project will automatically reference the new classification data.

What's Changing

The migration introduces the following high-level changes:

  • Takeoff-specific Classification Systems endpoints are being deprecated in favor of the Classifications API.
  • Takeoff API responses are being updated to reference classifications managed by the Forma Classifications Service.
  • New APIs are available for managing classification structures assigned to Takeoff projects.
  • 2D sheet references within the Takeoff API are moving from Sheets identifiers to Data Management file version URNs.

For complete technical details, including endpoint changes, payload updates, request/response examples, and migration guidance, refer to the Takeoff API Migration Guide.

 

Timeline

Date Milestone
July 22, 2026
  • Updated Takeoff API and Forma Classifications API are released.
  • Updated Takeoff API documentation and Migration Guide are published.
  • The deprecation process begins for the legacy classification endpoints and fields. They are now deprecated and will be removed after Jan 29, 2027.
Sep 1, 2026
  • Project-by-project migration begins.
Jan 29, 2027
  • All projects should be migrated.
  • Legacy classification fields (classificationCodeOne / classificationCodeTwo) and deprecated classification functionality are removed.

Project Migration

Migration is performed on a per-project basis.

During the rollout period, some projects may already use the new behavior while others continue using the legacy format. Integrations should support both formats until all of their projects have been migrated.

Detailed migration behavior is documented in the Takeoff API Migration Guide.

What You Should Do

If your application integrates with the Takeoff API, you should:

  • Review the Takeoff API Migration Guide for the complete list of API and payload changes.
  • Request a test project by emailing takeoff.migration.support@autodesk.com so you can validate your integration before the production migration.
  • Update your integration to support both legacy and migrated projects during the rollout period.
  • Complete your migration before January 29, 2027, when the deprecated functionality will be removed.

For details, please refer Takeoff API Migration Guide.

Who Is Affected?

You will need to update your integration if it uses any of the following:

  • Classification Systems endpoints
  • Classification data returned by the Takeoff API
  • classificationCodeOne or classificationCodeTwo
  • contentView.version for 2D takeoff items

If your integration does not use these capabilities, no action is required.

See the Takeoff API Migration Guide for the complete list of affected APIs and required migration steps.

Support

If you have questions about the migration or would like access to a test environment, please email takeoff.migration.support@autodesk.com to get direct support. Our team is happy to help you plan and validate your migration.

item.title: From Two Days to Two Minutes: How Khansaheb Turned Model Data into Commercial Intelligence
item.description:
From Two Days to Two Minutes: How Khansaheb Turned Model Data into Commercial Intelligence Anna Baranova

24 Jul 2026

Anna Baranova

Share

On a complex construction project, waiting on information is rarely just a small delay—often it can slow teams down, push decisions out, and break the flow of work.

That was the reality at Khansaheb Civil Engineering. Its commercial teams depended on accurate, up-to-date quantities for estimating, cost control, monthly measurement, and resource planning. But much of that information was buried inside BIM models. Accessing it meant submitting requests to the BIM team, waiting for manual exports, and often working with data that was already out of date by the time it arrived.

The existing workflow had created a bottleneck. BIM specialists were constantly pulled away from their core work, while commercial teams often had to wait longer than they should for the information they needed.

Khansaheb needed a way to publish structured model data directly into the business tools its commercial teams already used, rather than introducing another manual export workflow.

Autodesk Data Exchange provided that connection.

Each week, discipline-specific models are brought together and structured model data is published automatically to Microsoft Power BI. Commercial teams can open a dashboard they’re already comfortable with and explore up-to-date quantities—doors, slabs, blockwork, structural elements—without opening Revit or waiting for the BIM team to prepare another export.

The impact on speed has been hard to ignore. According to Khansaheb, tasks like sheet production, which used to take up to two days, now take less than two minutes—a reduction of more than 99%. Coordination issues that previously took over an hour can now be resolved in under ten minutes. Complex model-data calculations that once required days of manual work can be completed in less than a minute.

But the benefits go beyond faster reporting.

Giving commercial teams direct access to current model data changes how information moves through the project. Decisions can be made sooner, questions can be answered without waiting for a specialist, and errors or missing information are more likely to be spotted early. As more teams use the data, they also help improve its quality.

Khansaheb’s story is a strong example of what Data Exchange can make possible. It puts useful project information in the hands of the people who need it, without requiring every team to use the same application or workflow.

Learn more about this case in the full Khansaheb success story—and continue the conversation with Khansaheb and the Data Exchange team at Autodesk University.

Continue the Conversation at Autodesk University

Khansaheb will share more about its approach in the AU session:

From Chaos to Clarity: The Data Exchange Strategy Behind a $1.3B Dubai Harbour Icon

The session will explore the challenges behind the workflow, the decisions that shaped Khansaheb’s approach, and the role connected model data is playing in faster, more informed commercial decision-making.

It is one of several Data Exchange sessions at AU for teams interested in interoperability, connected workflows, and practical ways to make design and construction data more useful.
